theater: 河南滑縣與京師紫禁城

battle.name: 癸酉之變
battle.theater: 河南滑縣與京師紫禁城
battle.brief: 嘉慶十八年九月，天理教首林清與李文成在河南滑縣起兵，分路進逼京師。九月十五日癸酉日，約二百名教眾經東華門、西華門闖入皇城，宗室綿寧以火槍擊斃一人。城內靠燧發槍與步軍冷兵器抵禦，義軍旋即潰散；滑縣、曹縣、定陶一線的據點戰卻延續至翌年，清軍以綠營抬槍與鄉勇分路進剿。

kit.name: 燧發槍
kit.history: 擊錘打火比火繩穩。線性列陣的射速和精度都靠它撐著。

countries: 交戰一方是清廷及其編制下的中央禁軍與地方綠營、團練鄉勇。皇城防務由內大臣、領侍衛內大臣與都統一級的宗室王公主持，步軍營、護軍營、前鋒營分守內城與皇城諸門，內務府與內侍分掌宮禁鑰匙與門禁；外圍由直隸、山東、河南三省綠營兵會同各地練勇、團練及騎隊分路進剿，欽差大臣額勒登保、楊遇春、那彥成等分領各戰區，勒保、吳熊光、百齡先後以直隸總督、兩江總督身份坐鎮，軍機處與內閣承旨調度。另一方是華北天理教，即自八卦教分化出的秘密結社：教首林清號天王，自稱彌勒佛轉世，掌京城一線；李文成號人王，被推為明朝真主，掌河南滑縣一線；馮克善號地王，掌魯西南一線的拳械與鄉社網絡。三人之下按八卦分編徒眾，多為礦工、馬夫、炭夫、流民與失業旗丁，武器多為大刀、鐵棍與鳥槍，並在紫禁城內拉攏數名內侍作內應。官府定其為教匪，一律以剿辦論處。
countriesEn: One side was the Qing court together with the central palace guards and the provincial Green Standard army, drill corps and village braves. The defence of the palace was directed by the Grand Minister of the Household, the Minister of the Imperial Guards and Manchu officers of the rank of commandant, with the Foot Guard, Palace Guard and Vanguard Battalions holding the inner city and the several palace gates, while the Imperial Household Department and the eunuchs kept the keys of the forbidden quarter and the gate watches. Outside the capital, Green Standard troops from Zhili, Shandong and Henan operated with local drill corps, banner militia and mounted parties along several separate fronts; the imperial commissioners Eledengbao, Yang Yuchun and Nayancheng commanded the main columns, while Lebao, Wu Xiongguang and Bailing served as governor-general of Zhili or of the Liangjiang circuit, receiving their orders through the Grand Council and the Grand Secretariat. The other side was the Heavenly Principle Sect of North China, the secret society that had grown out of the Eight Trigrams sect. Its chief Lin Qing, styled King of Heaven and claiming to be Maitreya in rebirth, held the capital end of the network; Li Wencheng, styled King of Men and acclaimed as the true lord of the Ming, held the Henan end around Huaxian; and Feng Keshan, styled King of Earth, held the southwestern Shandong end together with his clubs and village associations. Beneath the three kings the followers were sorted into the eight trigrams and were mostly miners, carters, charcoal burners, vagrants and discharged banner soldiers, armed chiefly with broadswords, iron bars and matchlock muskets, and they had won over several eunuchs inside the Forbidden City to act as insiders. The court classified them as sect rebels and treated the business throughout as a campaign of suppression.
people: 核心人物是三王與清廷兩邊的將相。教首林清出身京師一帶市井，娶妻後轉入天理教，兩年間以行醫賣藥為名往來各縣，藉賑濟災民廣收門徒；起義事發時他並未親至皇城，只在城內坐鎮，事後被清廷列為首惡，嘉慶十九年初被捕，於菜市口凌遲處死。人王李文成是河南滑縣一帶的教門領袖，在滑縣聚眾起事，兵敗退保輝縣時在清軍圍攻下自焚而亡；其妻張氏接手滑縣防務，據城抵抗到嘉慶二十年城破之日自縊殉城，被清廷旌表。副手陳明經在北線兵敗被擒，同樣以凌遲處死；地王馮克善在舉事前已被官府緝獲下獄，未能與李、林同時起兵。清廷方面，宗室綿寧在皇城之亂中以自佩火槍擊斃一名叛者，成親王等率侍衛搜捕街巷；內大臣楊芳主持門禁與內城應變。嘉慶帝其時正在塞外木蘭行獵，聞變後於十月移駕熱河並下罪己詔。
peopleEn: The central figures are the three kings on one side and the commanders and ministers of the Qing court on the other. The sect chief Lin Qing came from the streets of the capital and joined the Heavenly Principle Sect after marrying, and for two years moved between counties under the guise of practising and selling medicine, gathering followers by distributing relief to the famine-stricken; when the rising broke out he did not take part in the attack on the palace in person but remained in the city, and was named the principal villain afterwards, arrested in the first month of the nineteenth year of Jiaqing and cut up at the Caishikou. Li Wencheng, the King of Men, was the sect leader around Huaxian in Henan; he raised his followers at Huaxian and, defeated, burned himself to death with his own hands while the Qing army besieged him at Huixian. His wife Zhang then took over the defence of Huaxian and held the city until it fell in the twentieth year of Jiaqing, when she hanged herself, and the court honoured her as chaste. His lieutenant Chen Mingjing was captured after the defeat of the northern columns and was likewise cut up; the King of Earth Feng Keshan had already been arrested and imprisoned before the rising and could not march with Li and Lin. On the Qing side the prince Mianning shot and killed one of the rebels with his own musket during the fighting in the palace, Prince Cheng and other princes led the guards in sweeping the streets, and the Grand Minister of the Household Yang Fang took charge of the gates and of the emergency inside the inner city. The Jiaqing Emperor was at that moment hunting beyond the Great Wall at Mulan; on hearing of the rising he moved his court to Jehol in the tenth month and issued a self-reproaching edict.
kits: 任務中的燧發槍在這一役的位置很特別：它不是綠營的制式步槍，而是宗室王公與禁軍上層用於自衛的精兵器，皇城之亂當夜，綿寧正是用自帶火槍在門內近距離擊斃一名叛者，說明清廷高層手中已有相當數量的個人燧發槍。制式重火器則是抬槍，一具要四至五人操持：一人扛槍身與支架，一人裝藥，一人點火，另需人扶肩助瞄，用於遠程覆蓋但不便隨隊前進；另有鳥槍、擲彈用的抬砲與邊軍仍在使用的火繩槍。冷兵器方面，禁軍配腰刀、長矛與小型盾牌，綠營與團練仍以腰刀、弓箭、長矛為主，騎隊用馬刀與角弓。義軍裝備與之成對比：以大刀、朴刀、鐵棍、長矛、叉為主，鳥槍數量有限，守城用滾木、礌石、檑木，攻城用雲梯、掘進的地道與火藥包爆破城門城根；糧草與軍械靠大車、騾馬運載，佔區內則取糧倉與漕運沿線的存糧。與此同時，官府收繳民間鳥槍、刀矛、弓矢，並禁毀會堂與拳棒器械，收繳來的鳥槍多被編入綠營使用。
kitsEn: The flintlock musket of this card occupies an unusual place in the campaign. It was not the standard musket of the Green Standard but a personal weapon carried by princes and senior officers of the palace guard for their own defence. On the night of the palace attack Mianning killed one of the rebels at close quarters with the musket he carried himself, which shows that the upper reaches of the Qing court already held a fair number of individual flintlocks. The standard heavy firearm was the rested musket, the tiaoqiang, which needed four or five men to work: one to carry the barrel and its rest, one to load, one to fire, and others to steady the shoulder while aiming. It covered long distances but was too heavy to advance with the line. There were also plain matchlock muskets, the hurling piece taipao, and the slow match used in the frontier garrisons. In cold weapons the palace guard carried waist swords, spears and small shields, while the Green Standard and the village militia relied on waist swords, bows and spears, the mounted parties on sabres and composite bows. The rebel equipment was the mirror image of this: broadswords, heavy sabres, iron bars, long spears and pitchforks, with only a limited number of matchlock muskets. For the defence of a town they used rolling logs, stones and dropped beams; for the attack they used scaling ladders, saps and gunpowder bags to blow the gates and the foot of the walls. Guns and provisions were moved by carts and mules, and in the area they held they took grain from the depots and from the stores along the canal. At the same time the authorities confiscated private matchlocks, blades, spears and bows, and banned the meeting halls and the boxing clubs; the muskets that were confiscated were mostly enrolled into the Green Standard.
tactics: 起義的部署是三路聯動。林清在京城收買內侍、勘察門路，選定九月十五日午間守軍用膳、宮門出入最鬆的時段，徒眾以白布纏頭纏腰為識別，事先埋伏在東華門、西華門內外的店鋪中，等內應開門後一湧而入；李文成在河南滑縣起事，取道北上一面擴散教門，一面打算與林清部會師於京師；馮克善在魯西南匯聚拳械好手與鄉社勢力，形成對省界的震懾。皇城之戰得以得手全靠內應與時機，守軍反應後立即關閉城門、結陣逐巷抵抗，宗室與侍衛帶槍搜索，叛者失去突擊優勢即各自潰散。野戰層面，義軍依靠村寨堡壘與堅牆固守，清軍則用圍城打援的辦法：分兵監視各門、斷絕糧道與援兵路，築營壘、挖壕溝封住水道，練勇在夜間掘地道逼近城牆，或以雲梯、炸藥強攻；義軍則利用運河與縣城之間的地理分割，遊擊遲滯清軍，以守待援。整個冬季的攻防，誰能先把糧道掐斷，誰就控制戰局。
tacticsEn: The rising was planned along three linked axes. In the capital Lin Qing bought the services of eunuchs and studied the approaches, and chose the fifteenth of the ninth month, the hour around noon when the guards ate and the palace gates were at their loosest. His followers wore white cloth round head and waist to identify each other and had already hidden in the shops inside and outside the eastern and western palace gates, waiting for the insiders to open the way so that they could pour in together. Li Wencheng rose at Huaxian in Henan and moved northward both to spread the sect and to converge with Lin Qing's men on the capital. Feng Keshan gathered skilled martial artists and village associations in southwestern Shandong, and it was his presence that terrorised the provincial borders. The palace attack succeeded only because of the insiders and the timing; once the guard recovered, the gates were shut at once, the line fought street by street, and princes and guards searched the quarter with their muskets, so that the rebels, deprived of the advantage of surprise, scattered. In the field the rebels relied on village strongholds and thick walls, while the Qing army used the classic siege-and-relieve method: separate columns watched every gate, the supply route and the roads by which relief could come, camps and trenches were dug to cut the water, the drill corps approached the walls by night in saps, or the walls were assaulted with ladders and powder. The rebels in turn exploited the geography between the canal and the county towns, harassing the Qing columns and standing on the defensive in the hope of relief. Across the whole winter of operations, whoever cut the supply route first controlled the field.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。襲擊皇城的義軍約二百五十人，其中約八十人在城門關閉前闖入內城；城內戰鬥結束時，義軍三十一人被擊斃，四十四人被俘。起義主力在滑縣一線集結時，報導所稱人數達數萬，但清廷諭旨與地方奏報多以數萬、十餘萬等概括字眼處理；李文成敗退輝縣時所帶約四千人。官方檔案記被剿殺的教眾逾二萬人，若連同各府縣練勇、鄉勇參戰造成的損失，後人統計約七萬上下，各版本分歧甚大，應視為量級而非精確值。時間線亦可對齊：嘉慶十八年七月教首議定起義日期，九月初二官府拘捕李文成，初六眾人仍在收集中武器，十五日癸酉襲皇城，十月十八日移駕熱河，翌年一月一日清軍攻破河南方面的總部據點，滑縣最後的據點則拖到嘉慶二十年才被攻下，張氏自縊。火器性能方面，燧發槍單兵射速約每分鐘一至三發，精度優於火繩槍且不怕風雨；抬槍一具需四至五人合用，射程雖遠卻不能隨隊前進；一名綠營步卒通常只配腰刀與長矛，火槍比例偏低。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are roughly as follows. About two hundred and fifty rebels took part in the attack on the palace, of whom some eighty forced their way through the gates before they were shut; when the fighting inside was over, thirty-one rebels had been killed and forty-four taken alive. When the main body of the insurgents mustered along the line of Huaxian, the numbers reported run to several tens of thousands, but the Qing edicts and provincial memorials deal in such round expressions as several ten thousands or a hundred thousand and more; Li Wencheng is said to have taken about four thousand men with him when he withdrew to Huixian. The official record has more than twenty thousand sect members killed in the suppression, and if the losses caused by the drill corps and village braves of the various prefectures are added, later reckonings put the total at around seventy thousand; the versions differ widely, and the figure should be read as an order of magnitude rather than an exact number. The chronology can also be aligned: in the seventh month of the eighteenth year of Jiaqing the chiefs fixed the date; on the second day of the ninth month the authorities arrested Li Wencheng, and on the sixth the followers were still collecting weapons; on the fifteenth, the day designated kuei-yu, the palace was attacked; on the eighteenth of the tenth month the court moved to Jehol; on the first of January in the following year the Qing army carried the headquarters position in Henan; the last position at Huaxian held out until the twentieth year of Jiaqing, when it fell and Zhang hanged herself. As for the firearms, a flintlock musket could be fired at a rate of roughly one to three rounds a minute by a trained man, was more accurate than the matchlock and did not fail in wind and rain; one rested musket required four or five men, and although its range was long it could not advance with the infantry; a Green Standard foot soldier was normally issued a waist sword and a spear, with muskets in relatively small proportion.
cause: 癸酉之變的起因是多層累積的。天理教是華北白蓮教的一支，帶有互相賑濟、扶病濟難的結社性質，乾隆朝以後清廷厲禁彌勒、白蓮等教門，社團轉入地下，卻始終沒有斷絕。嘉慶十六年天上出現明亮彗星，清廷看作國運之兆，教眾卻讀作起事之機。次年教首公開推舉河南滑縣的李文成為明朝真主，定一八一三年為舉事之年，林清則自稱彌勒佛轉世，三人分稱天王、人王、地王，構成完整的改朝框架。直接引爆的還有天災：華北連年旱澇，麥價飛漲，饑民大量依附教門結社，救濟名目下的信眾網絡迅速膨脹。1796 至 1804 年的白蓮教起義雖被鎮壓，清廷在直隸、山東、河南三省的巡查與保甲從未真正落實到基層，秘密教門反而在壓制中擴張。教眾更看準嘉慶帝例行赴塞外木蘭秋獵、皇城守備空虛的時機，把目標直接指向宮禁。九月二日李文成在北京被捕又遭同道劫出，暴露了起義的內情，逼得全體提前動作，九月十五日癸酉日按計畫發難。於是天象、災荒、教門、邊防空虛與官府失察疊在一起，構成了這一變的引爆點。
causeEn: The outbreak of the kuei-yu rising was the product of several layers of accumulation. The Heavenly Principle Sect was a North China branch of the White Lotus teaching, a mutual-aid society built on relieving the sick and helping the poor, and after the Qianlong reign the court had banned the cult of Maitreya and of White Lotus with great severity, driving the societies underground without ever destroying them. In the sixteenth year of Jiaqing a bright comet appeared in the sky; the court read it as an omen of dynastic glory, while the faithful read it as the moment for action. In the following year the leaders openly acclaimed Li Wencheng of Huaxian in Henan as the true lord of the Ming and fixed the year eighteen thirteen for the rising, while Lin Qing proclaimed himself the reincarnation of Maitreya; the three styled themselves King of Heaven, King of Men and King of Earth, and so completed a whole framework for a change of dynasty. Natural disaster lit the fuse: successive droughts and floods in North China sent the price of wheat soaring, the hungry clung to the sect's societies, and the network of believers spread rapidly under the banner of relief. Although the White Lotus rising of 1796 to 1804 had been suppressed, the patrol system and the community ward organisation of the court were never really enforced at village level in Zhili, Shandong and Henan, and the secret sects expanded under pressure. The believers also fixed on the moment when the Jiaqing emperor went annually hunting at Mulan beyond the Wall, leaving the capital lightly guarded, and turned their aim directly at the palace. On the second day of the ninth month Li Wencheng was arrested in the capital and was carried off again by his own followers, which exposed the conspiracy, forced the whole movement to act early, and brought the rising forward to the fifteenth of the ninth month, the day kuei-yu, as planned. Astronomy, famine, the sects, the empty border towns and the negligence of the officials thus piled together into the detonation.
impact: 癸酉之變對清廷的衝擊遠超一次地方教案。皇城為叛眾突入，是入關以來罕有的失守，京城震動、人心惶惑，嘉慶帝十月移駕熱河，隨即下罪己詔，詔書自責朝廷失察，並施恩赦免、停部分捐納以補財政虧空。事後的清算極為嚴酷：京師與直隸、山東、河南三省大索教門，連坐被處死者以萬計，官方記錄教眾被剿逾二萬，連同地方練勇、鄉勇參戰的損失，總數被統計為約七萬；教首林清、陳明經皆凌遲處死，李文成之妻張氏在城破之日自縊，清廷旌其烈節。地方官員成片被究：直隸、山東、河南各級因失察、匿報、通賊議處，總督、巡撫多人降調革職。制度層面的調整同樣深遠：內城門禁與鑰匙保管收緊，內侍監肅清，禁軍一部被調出京畿轉用於剿辦；地方上加強保甲、查禁會教與拳棒社團，天理教在原活動區從此一蹶不振。教禁亦殃及池魚，清廷借教案加強對洋教的查禁，廣東一帶正在起步的新教傳播受到擠壓。秘密宗教只能更深地轉入地下，直到更晚的年代才重新聚集。
impactEn: The shock the kuei-yu rising gave the Qing court was far greater than that of a local rising. That rebels forced their way into the palace was a breach without precedent since the Manchus entered the capital, and the city was shaken and the public alarmed; in the tenth month the Jiaqing emperor moved his court to Jehol and soon after issued a self-reproaching edict, in which the court blamed itself for having missed the sects, pardoned offenders and suspended part of the sale of offices in order to make up the fiscal shortfall. The reckoning afterwards was extremely harsh. A great sweep for sect members was carried out in the capital and in the three provinces of Zhili, Shandong and Henan, and the number put to death on the strength of collective responsibility ran into the tens of thousands; the official record gives more than twenty thousand sect members killed in the suppression, and with the losses inflicted by the drill corps and village braves the total was reckoned at about seventy thousand. The chiefs Lin Qing and Chen Mingjing were both cut up, and Li Wencheng's wife Zhang hanged herself on the day her city fell, and the court honoured her with a title. Provincial officials were punished in whole batches, being impeached, demoted or dismissed for negligence, for concealing information or for collusion with the rebels, and several governors-general and governors were removed from office. The institutional consequences were equally deep: the regulations on the gates of the inner city and on the keeping of the keys were tightened, the eunuch corps was purged, and part of the palace guard was transferred out of the metropolitan area to serve in the suppression. In the provinces the community ward system was reinforced and the meeting halls and boxing clubs were suppressed, and the Heavenly Principle Sect never recovered in the districts where it had been strongest. The suppression of the sects also dragged in foreign religion, since the court used the affair to tighten its restrictions on the western teaching, and the budding Protestant mission in Guangdong was squeezed. The secret religions could only sink deeper underground, and did not gather strength again until much later.
result: 結果分內外兩層。內城一役，叛眾因突擊時間有限、門禁受制、援兵不及，攻入者未能擴大戰果，城門關閉後被逐段清剿，擊斃三十一人、俘獲四十四人，無一人逃出城門；宗室綿寧以自佩火槍親手擊斃一人，嘉慶帝當時在塞外行獵，未遭刺殺，但京城受創已足以震動朝野。河南一線的抵抗則延續更久：義軍據滑縣、曹縣、定陶、濮州等地達半年以上，與清軍在寨牆、壕溝與糧道上反覆拉鋸；嘉慶十八年十二月李文成在輝縣自焚，翌年滑縣的最終據點被攻破，張氏自縊殉城，殘部或散或降。官府於翌年初宣布平定，但城破與大索一直延續到嘉慶二十年。清廷在軍事上輕易得手，代價卻是又一次的血流與鎮壓：數萬教眾被剿殺，數十名官員被處分，皇城失守的恥辱寫進了詔書。就白蓮教系列的起義而言，癸酉之變是規模最大、距京師最近、也是最後一次大規模爆發，此後教門在華北再無公開起事，直到更晚的年代才重新聚集力量。
resultEn: The outcome had an inner and an outer side. In the inner city the rebels, short of time, hampered by the closed gates and unsupported, could not enlarge their success; once the gates were shut they were hunted down street by street, thirty-one killed and forty-four captured, and not a single man escaped through the gates. The prince Mianning shot one rebel dead with his own musket, and the Jiaqing emperor, then hunting beyond the Wall, was not assassinated, though the wound to the capital was enough to shake the court. The resistance on the Henan front lasted far longer: the rebels held Huaxian, Caoxian, Dingtao and Puzhou for more than half a year, and fought the Qing army back and forth along palisades, trenches and supply routes; in the twelfth month of the eighteenth year of Jiaqing Li Wencheng burned himself at Huixian, and the last positions at Huaxian were carried in the year that followed, Zhang hanging herself as the city fell, the survivors scattering or surrendering. The authorities proclaimed the business suppressed in the first months of the following year, though sieges and sweeps continued into the twentieth year of Jiaqing. The Qing victory came easily on the field, and it was paid for in blood and in repression once more: tens of thousands of sect members were killed, dozens of officials were punished, and the shame of the breached palace was written into the imperial edict. Within the series of White Lotus risings, the kuei-yu rising was the largest, the closest to the capital and the last to break out on any scale; after it the sects staged no more open revolt in North China until a much later time.
